claims.statement: Meta documents an App Secret that Meta assigns to each Meta app, found in the App Dashboard basic settings, and that must be stored securely and kept out of client-side code.

sources.supports: find the app secret assigned to your app by Meta
It is extremely important that an App Secret be stored securely and not be included in any code that could be accessed by anyone other than a developer of the app.

claims.statement: Three open-source scanner rule artifacts by different maintainers (Gitleaks, TruffleHog, Nosey Parker) each treat a string of exactly 32 alphanumeric characters appearing next to a facebook-related context word as an application-secret candidate. This records consistency among those artifacts; it is not a provider statement of the format, and the artifacts differ on the alphabet (lowercase hexadecimal in one, wider alphanumeric sets in the other two).

sources.supports: Rule facebook-secret: a context word 'facebook' followed by an assignment-like separator and a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal capture group.
apiSecretPat: a 'facebook' prefix context followed by a word-bounded capture of exactly 32 alphanumeric characters.

Rule np.facebook.1 (Facebook Secret Key): a facebook or fb context word with app/secret/key words, then a word-bounded capture of exactly 32 lowercase alphanumeric characters (case-insensitive flag set).

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Only the existence and handling of the app secret are provider-documented; no Meta page read states its format. The 32-character length rests on a tool-corroborated claim (consistency among scanner rule artifacts) and the alphabet is not settled. Independence of the three artifacts' authors is a reviewer check, not a machine check. Resolve with a Meta page stating the format; a bare secret needs provider context and must not be attributed from shape.
